findings.title: Preference within a common gift
findings.claim: 17:12 first uses the focus root for bounty sought from the Lord; 17:20 then extends one unbarred gift to both contrasted orientations; 17:21 differentiates portions. Preference therefore occurs within shared receipt, not as a simple gate separating recipients from the denied, and present abundance alone does not certify approval.
findings.mechanism: The focus partitives and f-d-l comparison meet the preceding total inclusion, continued extension, gift, and explicit non-barring. The earlier bounty use supplies a root echo. Together these carriers move the reading from a binary admission model to differentiated shares inside one provision field.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see both the reality of unequal allocation and the separate fact of common receipt.
findings.containment: Universal gift may mean common creaturely support without specifying why shares differ. Neither receipt nor present abundance identifies final standing, and the HFT contribution remains legacy_unbound wherever its cross-root branch is unresolved.

epistemic.reason: The contextual relationship is HFT-attributed; the trusted channel nomination supplies exact source images for the three shared nominated branches.

The independent external trigger names the straight path and those upon whom favor has been bestowed, then contrasts them with angered and straying groups. findings.containment: This overlay is exploratory. It does not identify any group in 17:21 with a group in 1:7, establish a one-to-one rank scale, or make worldly privilege proof of divine favor. It adds a possible ethical axis, not a verdict.

epistemic.reason: The external ayah is supplied exactly, but the moral-path relation to the focus is interpretive and has no separate trust-labeled support record.
